descriptionHtml:
Decision D1 · P0 · Daniela

Live dictation audio goes from the browser straight to OpenAI with a 60-second token our server mints, not through our server — acceptable? (Q2)

Approach · OAT-05 Keeping Data Secure / Real-PHI Readiness Gate · S11 Speech-to-text routes: transcription value by path, authentication and BAA coverage, with the on-device marker locked to test accounts

UAT steps / ticket ACs covered:

  • U3a Speech-to-text runs through a BAA-covered, authenticated path, not a direct, unauthenticated call: routed server-side, with no API key in the browser. (UAT OAT-05 step 3; TFA-94423 AC 1)

Test design technique: Decision table (decision-table) — List the combinations of several conditions and check each one, to see that the result follows the rule.

Given The code at the UAT commit (convex/ai/transcribe.ts, convex/aiProvider.ts, convex/settings.ts update() and lib/authRows assertTestFixtureUser, src/lib/speech/liveSession.ts, src/lib/dictation.ts resolveDictationEngine, the Capacitor native speech plugin) and the production aiProvider.transcription value (from S19)

When Fill the table. (1) 'gpt-live', live capture: prepareSession, signed-in only, mints a 60 s secret; browser to api.openai.com/v1/realtime/calls; audio over WebRTC to OpenAI. (2) 'gpt-live', recovery of a kept recording: upload to Convex, then whisper-1. …

Then The row production uses is authenticated and reaches only an endpoint the OpenAI BAA covers. No row lets a real physician's audio reach a vendor without authentication or without coverage. The server refuses the on-device marker for an account outside roundai.test, any saved value resolves to the cloud engine, and the native speech plugin is never selected; …

Pass rule (oracle, excerpt): UAT OAT-05 step 3 'a BAA-covered path, not a direct, unauthenticated call', TFA-94423 AC 1 and AC 2, and Daniela on 2026-10-03 ('never directly from the browser … covered by a BAA'), carried into TFA-94423 and TFA-94700. A row that is unauthenticated, or that reaches an endpoint without confirmed coverage, is a Fail. …

Where it ran: local code-review (judged by reading the code); test method CODEREVIEW · Code review; lane planned in the matrix: manual (manual)

S11 is our own case number (its number in the coverage matrix cases/OAT-05.matrix.json), not a step number of the UAT document.

Triage (2026-10-14): 1 row; to be decided by Daniela; the Allure status was changed by the triage from unknown to failed.

Issue type: Needs a decision (Daniela) · environment local · tickets TFA-94423 ready for qa

Nothing a physician sees: during live dictation the audio streams from the browser straight to OpenAI over WebRTC, using a 60 s token our server mints, rather than through our server; whether direct-but-authenticated is acceptable is open (Q2).

Evidence: allure b9ca17c8-…-result.json; code-review lane, status fail-pending-Q2. Route 1 (gpt-live live capture) goes to api.openai.com/v1/realtime/calls with the server-minted secret. Recovery and whisper go through the server; voxtral/transcribe values are refused; the on-device marker is limited to @roundai.test accounts (whether that test-only native path is intended is also to confirm). Daniela said on 2026-10-03 'never directly from the browser'. BAA coverage (S08) and the production transcription value (S19, Tim) are other halves.

Environment: local — main e02167f, local stack (not a deployed build); run folder runs/2026-10-14-local, lane code-review.

Test method: CODEREVIEW · Code review; secondary: API · API (Convex functions) — as classified in cases/test-methods.json, which says it runs on local; Source: code-review.

UAT item: OAT-05 Keeping Data Secure / Real-PHI Readiness Gate · Section: B · Operational Acceptance Tests · Scenario: OAT-05/S11

Speech-to-text routes: transcription value by path, authentication and BAA coverage, with the on-device marker locked to test accounts

Tickets: TFA-94423 Implement GPT-live medical mode for active dictation (ready for qa)

New local lane code-review: status fail-pending-Q2 in code-review/results.json → needs a person (fails only on open question Q2, not counted as failed yet → a person looks).

Detail:

Route table from the code at e02167f:
(1) 'gpt-live', live capture: `prepareSession` is an `aiAction`, which calls `requireUserId`, so only a signed-in user can start it. The server holds OPENAI_API_KEY and mints a client secret that lasts 60 s. The browser then POSTs its SDP offer to https://api.openai.com/v1/realtime/calls with that secret, and the audio goes straight to OpenAI over WebRTC. It is authenticated but does not pass through our server.
(2) 'gpt-live', recovery of a kept recording: the recording is uploaded to the authenticated `transcribeAudio` action, which sends it to whisper-1 at https://api.openai.com/v1/audio/transcriptions from the server.
(3) 'whisper', or no row (`DEFAULT_TRANSCRIPTION = "whisper"`): `prepareSession` returns batch mode, and audio is uploaded through Convex to whisper-1 from the server.
(4) 'voxtral', 'transcribe', 'transcribe-medical': `transcriptionRoute` throws in its default branch, both in `prepareSession` and in `transcribeAudio`. These values are refused and nothing falls back to OpenAI.
(5) On-device test marker: `settings.update` calls `assertTestFixtureUser` when the value is "on-device-test", and that check only accepts an email ending in @roundai.test. `resolveDictationEngine` returns "cloud" for every other saved value. The native plugin is only reachable for engine "web-speech", which only the marker can produce, so a real account never reaches browser or native speech.
The question's pass rule would count row 1's short-lived server-minted secret as a pass. The oracle wins, and it judges row 1 (direct but authenticated) per Q2. That is the only point against the rule, so the verdict is pending:Q2. BAA coverage of each endpoint (S08), the production transcription value (S19) and the unit test results (static lane) belong to other halves.

Waits on open question (pendingOn):

  • Q2

Open questions (openQuestions):

  • Q2: is row 1 (gpt-live live capture, where the browser streams to api.openai.com/v1/realtime/calls using a server-minted 60 s secret, authenticated but not through the server) acceptable as 'a BAA-covered path, not a direct, unauthenticated call'? The question's pass rule would count a short-lived server-minted secret as a pass, but the oracle hands row 1 to Q2. That is why the verdict is pending, not pass.
  • The verdict also depends on which value production uses (S19). If production is 'whisper' or has no row, the route production uses is fully server-routed.
  • Q2: is row 1 (gpt-live: browser to api.openai.com/v1/realtime/calls with a 60 s server-minted secret, audio over WebRTC straight to OpenAI) an acceptable 'BAA-covered path, not a direct, unauthenticated call'? The question's pass rule allows a short-lived server-minted secret, but the oracle hands row 1 to Q2, so it is labelled pending:Q2.
  • The Then says 'the native speech plugin is never selected'. In the code, a roundai.test account holding the on-device marker on a native device would use the native plugin; real accounts never do. Confirm this test-only exception is intended.

Not decidable from the code (notDecidableByCode):

  • BAA coverage per endpoint (DOC (OAT-05/S08))
  • production aiProvider.transcription (CONFIG (OAT-05/S19, Tim))
  • unit tests (STATIC (static.mjs repo-checks))
  • Whether the OpenAI BAA covers /v1/realtime/calls (gpt-live-transcribe) and /v1/audio/transcriptions (whisper-1): S08, documents.
  • The production aiProvider.transcription value: S19, config, Tim.
  • Whether both unit tests pass: static lane (reported green at e02167f).
  • Whether OpenAI's BAA covers the /v1/realtime/calls and /v1/audio/transcriptions endpoints (S08).
  • The production aiProvider.transcription value, which decides which row production uses (S19).
  • Whether the unit tests are green: the static lane reports them passing at e02167f (context only).

Physician impact (physicianImpact): If production uses 'gpt-live', a physician's live dictation audio goes from their browser or device straight to OpenAI. The call is authorized by a 60-second server-issued credential, but the audio does not pass through the server. Whether that is acceptable waits on Q2. Every other route sends audio through the server, and a real account can never reach browser or native speech. / On the 'gpt-live' setting, a physician's live audio goes from their browser or app straight to OpenAI over WebRTC, using a 60-second secret minted by our server, rather than passing through our server. Whether that is acceptable waits on Q2 and on BAA coverage of that endpoint.

Review verdict (verdict): fail

Evidence: 2 attached.

Dev run: skipped: not runnable on dev — not-runnable-on-dev: scripted-spec, outside-runner (manual: doc-review). This local result replaces that dev entry (the scenario appears once).
